chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from al-Hasan ibn Nasr, from his father, from Abu Khalid al-Wasiti, who said:

We went to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) on a day of doubt regarding Ramadan, and found his table set while he was eating. We wanted to ask him, so he said, 'Come near for the midday meal. If it is like this day and the evidence of the crescent's sighting has not come to you, then do not fast.'

Then he said, 'My father Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) narrated to me from Ali (peace be upon him) that when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) became ill in his sickness, he said, "O people, indeed the year is twelve months, among them four are sacred."'

He said, then he gestured with his hand, 'That is Rajab al-Mufrad, Dhu al-Qadah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and al-Muharram; three are consecutive. And behold, this is the prescribed month, Ramadan. So fast upon its sighting and break your fast upon its sighting. When the month is obscured, complete the count: Sha'ban is thirty days, and fast the one and thirty.'
And he gestured with his hand, 'One, two, three; one, two, three, and he folds his thumb.'
Then he said, "O people, a month like this, and a month like this."
And Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'We fasted with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) for twenty-nine days and did not complete it, and saw it as complete.'

And Ali (peace be upon him) said, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Whoever adds a day to Ramadan intentionally from another month is not a believer in Allah and not in me.'

key_terms.أَيَّامُ تَمَامٍ: Days of completion (completing the month to thirty days)
key_terms.شَهْرٌ كَذَا وَ شَهْرٌ كَذَا: A month like this, and a month like this (gestural indication of thirty days)
key_terms.يَوْمُ الشَّكِّ: Day of doubt (the 30th of Sha'ban when sighting is uncertain)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for fasting on the day of doubt in Ramadan if the crescent is not sighted?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential status of *Yawm al-Shakk* (Day of Doubt) by linking Imam al-Baqir’s practice to the Prophet’s final instructions on lunar visibility, establishing that fasting is contingent upon actual sighting rather than calculation. It highlights the Shia emphasis on the physical evidence of the crescent and the Prophet’s specific hand gesture to count thirty days, reinforcing the principle of completing the count only when the sky is overcast or obscured. This narration serves as a primary proof for the Shia ruling that one does not fast on the 30th of Sha'ban if the moon is not seen, distinguishing it from the Sunni practice of presumptive fasting.
